items.text: JoltUI does not diff a virtual DOM. Templates declare which parts depend on which data, and when that data changes JoltUI re-evaluates just those parts. This page covers the data-bind mechanism and the three decorators built on it: @react, @reactFactory and @queryParam.

items.title: Bound regions
items.text:
Any element in a template can be marked with data-bind="<binding name>". When the component renders, JoltUI remembers the raw template of that element's contents. When the binding is invalidated, it evaluates the stored template again and replaces the element's contents.

override markup = () => html`
    <header>
        <h1>Inbox</h1>
        <span class="badge" data-bind="app.unread">
            {{= this.app.getData("unread") }}
        </span>
    </header>
    <message-list></message-list>
`;

Calling app.setData("unread", 3) anywhere in the application updates the badge and nothing else. The header, the heading and <message-list> are not touched.

Several elements may use the same binding name; they all refresh together. Regions can be nested: when the outer region refreshes, the inner one is rebuilt with it.

items.title: Binding names
items.text: Binding Invalidated by app.<field> app.setData("<field>", …) query.<name> a change of query parameter <name> through the App attr.<name> changing attribute data-jolt-<name> (or :<name>) on the component's host element any other name a @react / @reactFactory property, or this.invalidate(name)

items.title: Rules for bound regions
items.text:
A region is re-evaluated on its own, outside the context of the full template:

  • Reference only this and globals inside a region. Loop variables ({{~ list :item }}) and variables declared in {{ }} code outside the region do not exist when the region is refreshed. Put the loop inside the region, not the region inside the loop.
  • Use {{= }} and {{! }}, not ${}. Template-literal values are fixed when markup() runs.
  • Write the attribute with double quotes: data-bind="app.user".
  • Keep template code out of table structure. JoltUI stores a region's template by parsing it as HTML, and the HTML parser moves text that appears directly inside <table>, <tbody> or <tr> (such as a {{~ }} loop around rows) out of the table. The first render looks right; the refresh does not. Inside bound regions, build lists with <ul>/<li> or grid-styled <div> elements, or bind a region inside a table cell.
  • Child components inside a region are recreated when it refreshes. Keep stateful children outside frequently changing regions.

Event handlers inside a region keep working: the refreshed contents are hydrated again.

items.title: Application data: app.<field>
items.text:
override markup = () => html`
    <nav>
        <a href="/">Stories</a>
        <a href="/about">About</a>
        <div class="navbar-actions" data-bind="app.user">
            {{? this.app.getData("user") }}
                <a class="btn" href="/profile">Profile</a>
            {{??}}
                <a class="btn" href="/login">Sign in</a>
            {{?}}
        </div>
    </nav>
    <main id="page-content"></main>
`;

When the login page calls this.app.setData("user", user), the navigation updates without the layout or the page being re-rendered.

items.title: Query parameters: query.<name>
items.text:
Parameters changed with app.updateQueryParameters() or the queryParameters setter notify bindings named after the parameter:

override markup = () => html`
    <div class="filters">
        <button @click="setCategory" :category="All">All</button>
        <button @click="setCategory" :category="Design">Design</button>
    </div>

    <div data-bind="query.category">
        {{~ this.filteredPosts :post }}
            <article>{{! post.title }}</article>
        {{~}}
    </div>
`;

get filteredPosts(): Post[] {
    const category = this.app.queryParameters.category;
    return this.posts.filter(post => !category || post.category === category);
}

setCategory(_event: Event, args: { category: string }): void {
    this.app.updateQueryParameters({
        category: args.category === "All" ? null : args.category,
    });
}

The URL changes (?category=Design) and the list refreshes. Because the state is in the URL, it survives a reload and works with the Back button.

items.title: Attributes: attr.<name>
items.text:
A component can bind markup to its own host attributes. Whenever data-jolt-<name> changes on the host, regions bound to attr.<name> refresh:

@component({ tagName: "status-dot" })
export default class StatusDot extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    override markup = () => html`
        <span data-bind="attr.status">
            <i class="dot dot-{{= this.args.status }}"></i> {{= this.args.status }}
        </span>
    `;
}

const dot = this.querySelector("status-dot");
dot?.setAttribute(":status", "offline");   // refreshes the region
dot?.toggleAttribute(":status");           // removal also counts

setAttribute, removeAttribute and toggleAttribute all trigger the refresh, but only when the value actually changes. Only the contents of the bound element are re-evaluated, not its own attributes; put dynamic classes on an inner element.

items.title: Component state: @react
items.text:
@react(initialValue, bindingName?) turns an accessor field into reactive state. Assigning a new value invalidates the binding, which by default has the property's name:

import { react } from "joltui";

@component({ tagName: "todo-list" })
export default class TodoList extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    @react([] as string[])
    accessor items!: string[];

    @react("")
    accessor draft!: string;

    override markup = () => html`
        <form @submit="add">
            <input name="item" @input="typing" placeholder="New item">
            <button>Add</button>
        </form>
        <p data-bind="draft">Typing: {{! this.draft }}</p>
        <ul data-bind="items">
            {{~ this.items :item }}<li>{{! item }}</li>{{~}}
        </ul>
    `;

    typing(event: Event): void {
        this.draft = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value;
    }

    add(event: Event): void {
        event.preventDefault();
        if (!this.draft) return;
        this.items = [...this.items, this.draft];
        (event.currentTarget as HTMLFormElement).reset();
        this.draft = "";
    }
}
  • Each instance gets its own copy of the initial value, cloned with structuredClone, so @react([]) does not share one array between instances.
  • Assignment triggers, mutation does not. The setter compares values with Object.is. this.items.push(x) notifies nobody; write this.items = [...this.items, x], or call this.invalidate("items") after the mutation.
  • Custom binding names let one property drive a differently named region, or several properties share one: @react(0, "totals").
  • The accessor keyword is required. It is part of the standard decorators proposal and lets the decorator intercept reads and writes.

items.title: Non-cloneable initial values: @reactFactory
items.text:
structuredClone cannot copy functions, class instances with private state or DOM nodes. For such values, supply a factory that produces a fresh value for every instance:

import { reactFactory } from "joltui";

@reactFactory(() => new Map<number, Post>())
accessor postCache!: Map<number, Post>;

@reactFactory(() => new ShoppingCart(), "cart")
accessor cart!: ShoppingCart;

items.title: Manual invalidation
items.text:
this.invalidate(name) refreshes every region bound to name in this component. Use it for state that is not held in a decorated property:

private readonly selected = new Set<number>();

toggle(_event: Event, args: { id: number }): void {
    if (!this.selected.delete(args.id)) this.selected.add(args.id);
    this.invalidate("selection");
}

items.title: Query parameters as properties: @queryParam
items.text:
@queryParam(name, defaultValue?, bindingName?) exposes a query parameter as a string property. Reading it returns the current value (or the default); writing it calls app.updateQueryParameters():

import { queryParam } from "joltui";

@page({ path: "/search", title: "Search" })
@component({ tagName: "search-page" })
export default class SearchPage extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    @queryParam("q", "", "query.q")
    accessor q!: string;

    @queryParam("page", "1", "query.page")
    accessor page!: string;

    override markup = () => html`
        <input value="{{! this.q }}" @change="search">
        <div data-bind="query.q">Results for "{{! this.q }}"</div>
        <nav data-bind="query.page">
            Page {{= this.page }}
            <button @click="next">Next</button>
        </nav>
    `;

    search(event: Event): void {
        this.q = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value;
        this.page = "1";
    }

    next(): void {
        this.page = String(Number(this.page) + 1);
    }
}

Setting the property to null removes the parameter (declare the property as string | null and omit the default to allow that).

Which binding name?

Writing the property already fires the query.<name> event through the App. If you omit the third argument, the decorator additionally invalidates a local binding called query-<name>. Passing "query.<name>" as the binding name, as above, avoids the second refresh and keeps one consistent name for every region that depends on the parameter.

items.title: Choosing a tool
items.text: Situation Tool State shared by several components application data + app.<field> bindings State that belongs in the URL (filters, paging, tabs) @queryParam or updateQueryParameters + query.<name> State local to one component @react / @reactFactory A parent configuring a child at runtime host attributes + attr.<name> One component telling another to act a direct method call Anything else a plain field + invalidate(name) The whole component depends on one data field dataField in @component

items.title: Routing
items.text: The Router maps URLs to pages, renders the right layout chain and page, checks authentication and keeps the browser history in sync. You configure it by subclassing it and returning an instance from the App's routerGenerator().

items.title: Configuring the router
Supplying pages manually
items.text:
Without the Vite plugin, list the pages explicitly:

import AboutPage from "./pages/aboutPage.js";
import HomePage from "./pages/homePage.js";
import PostPage from "./pages/postPage.js";

const pages = [HomePage, PostPage, AboutPage] as const;

return new MyRouter({
    app: this,
    pages,
    baseLayout: MainLayout,
    defaultTarget: "#page",
});

items.title: Declaring pages
items.text:
@page accepts either a path or a configuration object:

@page("/about")

@page({
    path: "/posts/<int:postId>",
    title: "Story",
    layout: ReadingLayout,      // instead of the base layout
    target: "#article",         // instead of the default target
    subLayouts: [],             // see Layouts
    extras: { breadcrumb: "Stories" },
})
Option Meaning path URL pattern; must start with /. title Document title (passed through titleGenerator). layout Layout class for this page; defaults to the router's base layout. target Selector receiving the page; defaults to defaultTarget. subLayouts Ordered chain of nested layouts (Layouts). extras Free-form metadata, available as router.currentRoute.extras.

items.title: Route parameters
items.text:
Path segments written as <type:name> are parameters:

Pattern Matches Value <str:slug> any single segment decoded string <int:id> digits only number 
@page({ path: "/users/<int:userId>/posts/<str:slug>", title: "Post" })
@component({ tagName: "user-post-page" })
export default class UserPostPage extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    get userId(): number {
        return this.app.router.routeParameters.userId as number;
    }

    get slug(): string {
        return this.app.router.routeParameters.slug as string;
    }

    override markup = () => html`
        <h1>Post {{! this.slug }} by user {{= this.userId }}</h1>
    `;
}

The parameters are also available as app.currentRouteParameters. They are published only after authorization succeeds, and before any of the route's components start initializing, so BEFORE_INIT hooks and markup() can rely on them.

Paths are normalized before matching: repeated slashes are collapsed and a trailing slash is removed, so /users//42/ matches /users/<int:userId>.

items.title: Which route wins?
items.text:
When several patterns could match, the router prefers the most specific one. It compares, in order:

  1. more literal segments;
  2. fewer parameters;
  3. more int parameters than str parameters;
  4. segment by segment, literal before int before str;
  5. declaration order.
@page("/posts/new")           // 1st: two literal segments
@page("/posts/<int:id>")      // 2nd: int is more specific than str
@page("/posts/<str:slug>")    // 3rd

/posts/new opens the editor, /posts/42 the post with id 42 and /posts/hello-world the slug lookup. Two pages with the same path are a configuration error.

items.title: Links
items.text:
The router intercepts clicks on <a> elements inside the app container and navigates without reloading, provided that:

  • the link points to the same origin;
  • it is a plain left click without Ctrl, Meta, Shift or Alt;
  • the event was not already cancelled (preventDefault);
  • the link has no target="_blank", no download and no router-ignore attribute, and is not a mailto: or tel: link.
<a href="/posts/42">Read the story</a>              <!-- router -->
<a href="/legacy/report" router-ignore>Report</a>   <!-- full page load -->
<a href="/files/report.pdf" download>PDF</a>        <!-- browser -->

items.title: Programmatic navigation
items.text:
await this.app.router.redirect("/posts/42");
await this.app.router.redirect(`/login?target=${encodeURIComponent(path)}`);

redirect() pushes a history entry and resolves when the new page has rendered (or the navigation failed and the error handlers have run).

items.title: Back and Forward
items.text: The router listens to popstate, routes the restored URL and restores the scroll position recorded when the user left that entry.

items.title: Overlapping navigations
items.text:
When a navigation starts while another is still running (for example while an authentication check or a slow page is pending), the latest navigation wins:

  • the older navigation stops waiting at its next step and cannot commit its page, title, route parameters or current route;
  • elements it had already created are removed, which aborts their lifetime signals (Cancellation);
  • layouts from a completed navigation are kept and reused.

Asynchronous work that your own hooks started (a slow isAuthenticated, a titleGenerator call) may still finish in the background; the router ignores its result. Application-owned side effects within those hooks must be managed by the application.

items.title: Route events
items.text:
The router dispatches three bubbling events on the app container:

Constant Event name When routeEventsEnum.START route-change.start rendering of a route begins routeEventsEnum.LAYOUT_CHANGE_FINISHED route-change.layout-change.finished a new base layout has been rendered routeEventsEnum.FINISHED route-change.finished the page has rendered and the title is set

A layout can use them to highlight the active navigation link:

import { Lifecycle, lifecycle, routeEventsEnum } from "joltui";

@lifecycle(Lifecycle.AFTER_INIT)
trackActiveLink(): void {
    this.app.addEventListener(
        routeEventsEnum.FINISHED,
        () => this.markActiveLink(),
        { signal: this.abortSignal },
    );
}

markActiveLink(): void {
    for (const link of this.querySelectorAll<HTMLAnchorElement>("nav a")) {
        link.classList.toggle("active", this.app.router.urlIsCurrentPath(link.href));
    }
}

urlIsCurrentPath(href) compares the normalized path of href with the current route.

items.title: Document titles
items.text:
After a page has rendered, the router sets document.title. By default it uses the page's title. Override titleGenerator(tagName, title) to compute titles, for example to translate keys:

const translations = new Map([
    ["pages.stories", "True Stories"],
    ["pages.about", "About"],
]);

export default class MyRouter extends Router<MyApp> {
    override titleGenerator(tagName: string, title: string | null): string {
        if (!title) return this.app.appName;
        return translations.get(title) ?? title;
    }
}

titleGenerator may also return a promise. If it returns an empty value the original title is used, and if that is empty too the title is left unchanged. The special title "_default" sets the document title to the application name. router.setTitle(text) sets a title directly.

items.title: Inspecting the current route
items.text:
Member Description currentRoute The matched route: path, pattern, parameters, title, extras, handler, layout, subLayouts, … (null while an error page is shown) routeParameters Parameters of the current route queryParameters Same as app.queryParameters routes, routesMap The route table baseLayout, defaultTarget, baseUrl, indexRoute Configuration 
const breadcrumb = this.app.router.currentRoute?.extras.breadcrumb;

items.title: Base URLs
items.text:
An application often lives below a fixed prefix, sometimes one that itself contains parameters such as a tenant or a language. baseUrl prefixes every page path and supports the same <str:…> and <int:…> parameters:

return new MyRouter({
    app: this,
    baseLayout: MainLayout,
    defaultTarget: "#page",
    baseUrl: "/portal/<str:tenant>/<str:language>",
});

@page("/search")     // registered as /portal/<str:tenant>/<str:language>/search

Base parameters appear in routeParameters next to the page's own. Links in templates must contain the full URL:

<a href="/portal/{{= this.app.router.routeParameters.tenant }}/en/search">Search</a>

redirect() can build the prefix for you. With useBaseUrl: true, the base URL is prepended and its parameters are filled from the current route, optionally overridden:

// stay in the current tenant and language
await this.app.router.redirect("/search", { useBaseUrl: true });

// switch language
await this.app.router.redirect("/search", {
    useBaseUrl: true,
    baseParameters: { language: "sl" },
});

A missing, empty or (for int) non-integer base parameter throws a RouteParametersError. Without useBaseUrl the path is used exactly as given.

items.title: When no route matches
items.text: An unknown path raises a RouteNotFoundError, which goes to the error handlers like any other error. The usual response is to render a not found component in place without changing the URL with router.showErrorPage().

items.title: Server components
items.text: JoltUI renders on the client, but a component's template does not have to come from the client. A component can ask a server for its markup; the server decides what is shown, and the client class provides behaviour.

items.title: Setting up
items.text:
Configure the endpoint on the App and opt components in with useServer:

const app = new MyApp({
    appName: "Portal",
    serverComponentsUrl: "/api/components",
});

@component({
    tagName: "account-summary",
    groupName: "account",
    useServer: true,
})
export default class AccountSummary extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    refresh = async (): Promise<void> => {
        await this.rerender();
    };
}

<account-summary :currency="EUR"></account-summary>

items.title: The request
items.text:
To render, the component sends a POST request to serverComponentsUrl?<current query string> with credentials included and a JSON body:

{
    "tagName": "account-summary",
    "groupName": "account",
    "routeParameters": { "accountId": 42 },
    "queryParameters": { "tab": "overview" },
    "attributes": { "currency": "EUR" }
}

attributes contains the component's arguments (this.args, from its data-jolt-* attributes). groupName defaults to "default". The server identifies the component by tagName (and groupName, if it organises templates in groups) and answers with HTML.

Patera

The Patera Python framework implements this endpoint in its patera-joltui extension, with typed group and component handlers.

items.title: The response is a template
items.text:
The returned HTML is treated exactly like the output of markup(). doT expressions are evaluated with the client component as this, @event and :argument shorthands are expanded, and event handlers are bound to the client class's methods:

<!-- returned by the server -->
<section class="summary">
    <h2>Balance: 1,204.50 EUR</h2>
    <button @click="refresh">Refresh</button>
    <p data-bind="app.user">Signed in as {{! this.app.user?.name }}</p>
</section>

Server components can contain bindings and child components like any other template.

items.title: Failures
items.text:
Response Error network failure NetworkError 400 ServerComponentBadRequestResponse 401 AuthenticationError 403 AuthorizationError 404 ServerComponentNotFound 5xx InternalServerError any other non-2xx HttpRequestError 2xx with an empty or unreadable body MarkupFetchError

The error fails the component's initialization (or rejects rerender()) and reaches the error handlers as usual. A missing serverComponentsUrl is reported as a configuration error.

items.title: Customising the request
items.text:
fetchHTML(request, options) performs the request. It is an instance property rather than a prototype method, so super.fetchHTML is not available. To extend it, capture the inherited function in the constructor and wrap it:

@component({ tagName: "price-list", useServer: true })
export default class PriceList extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    constructor() {
        super();
        const baseFetchHTML = this.fetchHTML;
        this.fetchHTML = async (request, options = {}) =>
            await baseFetchHTML(
                {
                    ...request,
                    attributes: {
                        ...request.attributes,
                        locale: this.app.getData("locale"),
                    },
                },
                options,   // always forward: carries the signal and cache settings
            );
    }
}

Always forward options: they contain the abort signal and the cache settings. The cache key is computed from the request before your override changes it; if the added value affects the response, include it in templateCacheKey() too.

items.title: Prefetching
items.text:
prefetchHTML(request, options?) loads a server template into the cache ahead of time. It uses an independent request that is not tied to any component's lifetime:

@lifecycle(Lifecycle.AFTER_INIT)
warmUpDetails(): void {
    void this.prefetchHTML({ tagName: "order-details", groupName: "orders" });
}

When an <order-details> element with matching parameters renders later, its template comes from the cache.

items.title: Template caching
items.text: Any template, from the server or from markup(), can be cached so that it is not produced again for every instance.

items.title: Enabling the cache
items.text:
Caching is opt-in per component:

@component({ tagName: "about-page", cache: true, cacheDuration: 300 })

Without cacheDuration the App's templatesCacheDuration (default 300 seconds) applies. A duration of 0 disables caching for the component.

const app = new MyApp({
    appName: "Example",
    templatesCacheDuration: 300,
    templatesCacheCleanupInterval: 60,
});

items.title: What is cached
items.text:
The cache stores the template: the string returned by markup(), or the HTML returned by the server. It does not store the rendered result. doT expressions ({{= }}, {{? }}, {{~ }}) are still evaluated on every render with the component's current state, and bindings still work.

What the cache freezes is everything that went into producing the template:

  • values interpolated with ${};
  • data that an asynchronous markup() fetched;
  • the server's response.

That makes caching most valuable for server components and for markup() methods that do expensive work:

@component({ tagName: "country-select", cache: true, cacheDuration: 3600 })
export default class CountrySelect extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    override markup = async () => {
        const response = await fetch("/api/countries");
        const countries: Country[] = await response.json();
        return html`
            <select name="country">
                ${countries.map(country =>
                    `<option value="${country.code}">${country.name}</option>`,
                ).join("")}
            </select>
        `;
    };
}

The country list is fetched once an hour, however many forms show the selector.

Do not tie cached work to one component

The cached factory runs once and its result is shared. Passing this.abortSignal to the request above would let the removal of one component cancel work that other instances are waiting for. JoltUI itself cancels only each component's wait for a shared result, never the shared work.

items.title: Cache keys
items.text:
The default key combines:

  • the tag name;
  • the current route parameters;
  • the current query parameters (sorted);
  • the component's arguments;
  • for server components, also the group name.

Two instances with different arguments, or the same component on different URLs, get different cache entries. Application data is not part of the key, and setData() does not invalidate cached templates.

If the template depends on something else, such as the user's locale or permissions, override templateCacheKey(). It must return a non-empty string:

override templateCacheKey(): string {
    const locale = this.app.getData<string>("locale");
    return `catalog:${locale}:${this.args.category}`;
}

For server components, the method receives the outgoing request as a parameter.

items.title: Concurrency
items.text: If several components request the same key at once, they share one in-flight operation. A component removed while waiting stops waiting, but the shared request continues for the others and still populates the cache.

items.title: Invalidation and cleanup
items.text:
The application decides when cached templates become invalid: login, logout, an account switch, a permission change, or an update to data the templates are built from:

this.app.setData("user", null);
this.app.clearTemplatesCache();
Member Purpose clearTemplatesCache() Remove every entry. Requests already running finish for their callers but cannot repopulate the cache. removeCachedTemplate(key) Remove one entry. cleanTemplatesCache() Remove expired entries now; returns how many were removed. templatesCacheCleanupInterval Seconds between automatic cleanups (0 = off); can be changed at runtime. templatesCacheDuration Default lifetime in seconds; can be changed at runtime. getCachedTemplate, setCachedTemplate, getOrSetCachedTemplate Low-level access for custom caching.

Expired entries are also removed lazily when they are requested.

Clearing the cache does not abort network requests or re-render components already on screen. After an account change, also navigate away from or re-render the affected components; their lifetime signals cancel their existing work.

items.title: Templates
items.text: JoltUI templates are HTML strings evaluated by an extended version of the doT template engine. doT compiles a template into a JavaScript function; JoltUI calls that function with the component as this. Anything reachable from the component (its properties, getters, this.app, this.args) can be used in an expression.

items.title: Syntax at a glance
items.text: Syntax Meaning {{= expr }} Insert the value of expr as-is. {{! expr }} Insert the value of expr, HTML-encoded. {{ code }} Run JavaScript statements (declare variables, call functions). {{? cond }} … {{?}} Conditional block. {{?? cond }} else if inside a conditional. {{??}} else inside a conditional. {{~ list :item }} … {{~}} Loop over an array. {{~ list :item :i }} … {{~}} Loop with an index variable. {{## def.name: … #}}, {{# def.name }} Compile-time partials (define, then use).

items.title: Interpolation
items.text:
override markup = () => html`
    <h1>{{= this.post.title }}</h1>
    <p class="meta">By {{= this.post.author }} · {{= this.post.readTime }}</p>
    <img src="{{= this.post.cover }}" alt="">
`;

Expressions can be arbitrary JavaScript: method calls, ternaries, padStart, toLocaleString and so on. An expression that evaluates to undefined prints the text undefined, so supply defaults where needed:

<input name="search" value="{{! this.app.queryParameters.search ?? '' }}">

items.title: Escaping and security
items.text:
{{= }} inserts values without escaping. That is right for trusted values and for HTML you build deliberately, but not for text that a user or an external system controls. For those, use {{! }}, which encodes &, <, >, ", ' and /:

<!-- comment text comes from other users: encode it -->
<p class="comment">{{! comment.text }}</p>

<!-- the post title comes from our own CMS: raw output is fine -->
<h2>{{= post.title }}</h2>

Rule of thumb

Anything that originated outside your code (form input, query parameters, API data from other users) goes through {{! }}. Using {{= }} on such values opens the door to cross-site scripting.

items.title: Conditionals
items.text:
{{? this.user }}
    <a href="/profile">Hello, {{! this.user.name }}</a>
{{?? this.loading }}
    <span class="spinner"></span>
{{??}}
    <a href="/login">Sign in</a>
{{?}}

items.title: Loops
items.text:
<ul class="post-list">
    {{~ this.posts :post :index }}
        <li class="{{= index % 2 ? 'odd' : 'even' }}">
            <a href="/posts/{{= post.id }}">{{! post.title }}</a>
        </li>
    {{~}}
</ul>

The array expression is evaluated once; post and index are local variables inside the loop body.

items.title: Code blocks
items.text:
{{ ... }} runs statements. Variables declared there are visible for the rest of the template:

{{ const featured = this.posts.find(post => post.featured); }}
{{? featured }}
    <a class="featured" href="/posts/{{= featured.id }}">{{! featured.title }}</a>
{{?}}

items.title: Whitespace and comments
items.text:
To keep output compact, doT removes line breaks and tabs from the template before compiling it:

  • Do not use // comments inside {{ }} code. Once line breaks are gone, a line comment swallows the rest of the template. Use /* ... */; block comments are removed entirely.
  • Line breaks in the template disappear, including inside <pre> elements. Generate preformatted content through an expression ({{! this.source }}) so that the line breaks come from data rather than from the template text.

items.title: Event and argument shorthands
items.text:
After evaluation, JoltUI rewrites two attribute shorthands inside every opening tag:

You write JoltUI produces Purpose @click="save" jolt-click="save" Event binding :post-id="7" data-jolt-post-id="7" Argument

The rewrite is aware of HTML structure. It ignores comments, CDATA sections and the contents of <script>, <style>, <textarea>, <title> and similar raw-text elements, and touches only attribute names, never attribute values or text. user@example.com or a CSS rule such as a:hover is left alone. Names must be lowercase and may contain hyphens.

items.title: Templates outside markup
items.text:
Thanks to the patched DOM, the template engine is available wherever HTML is inserted into a component:

addDraft(): void {
    this.querySelector("#drafts")?.insertAdjacentHTML("afterbegin", html`
        <article class="draft">
            <h2>{{! this.newTitle }}</h2>
            <button @click="removeDraft">Remove</button>
        </article>
    `);
}

The inserted HTML is evaluated with the component as this, its shorthands are expanded and its event handlers are attached. The same holds for assigning innerHTML or outerHTML of any element owned by the component.

items.title: Partials with def
items.text:
doT's compile-time definitions repeat a fragment within one template. Define it once with {{## def.name: … #}} and insert it with {{# def.name }}:

{{## def.newBadge:
    <span class="badge">{{= this.isNew ? "new" : "" }}</span>
#}}

<h2>Articles {{# def.newBadge }}</h2>
<h2>Videos {{# def.newBadge }}</h2>

The fragment is copied into the template before compilation, so it can refer to this. Only the parameterless form is supported; doT's parameterised partials ({{## def.badge:label: … #}}) fail to compile.

For anything reused across components, a small component or a TypeScript helper function that returns a string is usually clearer.

items.title: Vite plugin
items.text: Listing every page in the router configuration is tedious and easy to get wrong. joltui-vite-plugin discovers pages at build time and hands them to the router automatically.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
npm install --save-dev joltui-vite-plugin
vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import joltui from "joltui-vite-plugin";

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [joltui()],
});

With the plugin in place, the router needs no pages option:

return new MyRouter({
    app: this,
    baseLayout: MainLayout,
    defaultTarget: "#page",
});

items.title: How it works
items.text:
1. Scan. The plugin parses every TypeScript file below src (or the Vite root if there is no src) with the TypeScript compiler API. It looks for classes decorated with @page and @component imported from joltui.
  2. Generate. It creates a virtual module, virtual:joltui-pages, that statically imports every discovered page and passes the list to registerGeneratedPages().
  3. Inject. It adds an import of the virtual module to the application entry (src/main.ts by default), so the pages are registered before the App starts.
  4. Use. When a Router is constructed without pages, it calls getGeneratedPages() and builds its route table from the result.

Conceptually, the generated module looks like this:

import Page0 from "/src/app/pages/aboutPage.ts";
import Page1 from "/src/app/pages/homePage.ts";
import Page2 from "/src/app/pages/postPage.ts";
import { registerGeneratedPages } from "joltui";

const pages = [Page0, Page1, Page2];
registerGeneratedPages(pages);
export default pages;

items.title: Rules for discoverable pages
items.text:
A page is discovered when its module:

  • imports page and component from joltui (named imports, renamed imports such as page as route, and namespace imports like import * as jolt from "joltui" with @jolt.page(...) all work);
  • declares the class as the module's default export: export default class …;
  • gives the class a name;
  • applies both @page and @component to it;
  • contains at most one page.
src/app/pages/homePage.ts
import { CustomElement, component, html, page } from "joltui";

@page({ path: "/", title: "Home" })
@component({ tagName: "home-page" })
export default class HomePage extends CustomElement<MyApp> {
    override markup = () => html`<h1>Home</h1>`;
}

items.title: Build-time validation
items.text:
The plugin turns these mistakes into build errors instead of runtime surprises:

  • a @page class that is not the default export (named exports are rejected, not ignored);
  • a page without @component;
  • an anonymous page class;
  • more than one page in a module;
  • two pages declaring the same static path;
  • two components declaring the same static tagName, anywhere in the scanned sources;
  • no pages at all.

Paths and tag names are checked when they are written as string literals, which is the normal case.

items.title: Options
items.text:
joltui({
    root: "src",
    entry: "main.ts",
    include: ["**/*.ts"],
    exclude: ["**/*.test.ts"],
    frameworkPackage: "joltui",
});
Option Default Meaning root src if it exists, else the Vite root Directory to scan, relative to the Vite root. entry main.ts, main.tsx, main.js Entry file(s), relative to root, that receive the virtual import. include **/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/*.mts Glob patterns to scan. exclude .d.ts, .test.*, .spec.*, node_modules, dist Glob patterns to skip. frameworkPackage joltui Package that exports page, component and registerGeneratedPages.

Scoped package names

If you install JoltUI under another name (for example from a private registry as @scope/joltui), set frameworkPackage to that name so the plugin recognises the imports.

items.title: Development and watch mode
items.text:
During vite development, adding, removing or changing a page declaration triggers a full page reload. Hot replacement is not possible because the browser cannot unregister a custom element once it has been defined.

vite build --watch is supported too. The plugin watches the source tree for new files, and every watch build rescans the sources and regenerates the virtual module, so creating, deleting or fixing a page is picked up without restarting the watcher.

items.title: Pages are eager, their dependencies lazy
items.text: Discovered pages are static imports and end up in the main bundle. Lazy dependencies declared by those pages remain separate chunks loaded on demand. Keep page classes thin and move heavy components and libraries into lazy dependencies.

items.title: Without the plugin
items.text: The plugin is a convenience, not a requirement. Pass pages to the router yourself, or call registerGeneratedPages([...]) from your own code before the App starts. getGeneratedPages() returns whatever was registered last.

items.title: Without a router
items.text:
routerGenerator() returns null by default. An App without a router is still useful: it can host components embedded in a server-rendered page, giving them shared data, templates, events and error handling without client-side routing.

import { App } from "joltui";

export default class WidgetsApp extends App<WidgetsApp> {}

items.title: Initialization order
items.text:
A custom element initializes as soon as it is both defined and connected, and it must find the [app-id] container at that moment. When the tags are already present in the server's HTML, initialize the App first and import the component modules afterwards:

<div id="widgets">
    <search-box></search-box>
    <cart-summary></cart-summary>
</div>

const app = new WidgetsApp({
    appName: "Widgets",
    dataStructure: { cart: [] },
});
await app.init("#widgets");

// Defining the elements now upgrades the tags already in the page.
await import("./components/searchBox.js");
await import("./components/cartSummary.js");

The same rule explains why pages and layouts can be imported statically in a routed application: they enter the DOM only when the router renders them, which happens after the container has been set up.

items.title: Progressive enhancement
items.text: Components without a markup method keep the HTML the server rendered into them and only attach behaviour (prerendered markup). Combined with an App without a router, this turns server-rendered pages into interactive ones without rewriting their templates on the client.

items.title: Development setup
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/MarkoSterk/joltui.git
cd joltui
npm install
Command Purpose npm run dev Start the Fieldnotes demo application (dev/) with Vite. npm run typecheck Type-check the framework. npm run build Compile src/ into dist/. npm run test:router Build and run the router tests. npm run test:cancellation Build and run the cancellation tests. npm run dev:build Production build of the demo application.

A Husky pre-commit hook runs npm run typecheck before each commit.

items.title: Pull requests
items.text:
• Keep changes focused and describe the user-visible effect.
  • Add or update tests for behaviour changes.
  • Update the documentation in docs/ in the same pull request when public behaviour changes; see Writing the documentation.

items.title: Writing the documentation
items.text:
The documentation is built with Zensical from the Markdown files in docs/ and the configuration in zensical.toml at the repository root. Versions are published with Zensical's fork of mike to the gh-pages branch and served by GitHub Pages.

Zensical is a Python tool. It runs through uv's uvx, so nothing is added to package.json; you only need uv and git.

items.title: Preview and build
items.text:
Run from the repository root:

uvx zensical serve           # http://localhost:8000, live reload
uvx zensical build --clean   # static site in site/

or with the wrappers:

BashPowerShell 
./scripts/docs.sh serve
./scripts/docs.sh build

.\scripts\docs.ps1 serve
.\scripts\docs.ps1 build

site/ and .cache/ are build output; keep them out of version control.

items.title: Structure
items.text:
Folder Content Style getting-started/ installation and a first application step by step, for newcomers guide/ one page per part of the framework explains concepts with examples deployment.md building and hosting checklist reference/ configuration, decorators, classes, events, errors, exports complete, terse look-up project/ versioning, contributing, these notes, license assets/ logo, diagrams, stylesheets/extra.css

Add a new page to the nav in zensical.toml, or it will not appear in the navigation.

  • Keep examples consistent with the Fieldnotes demo in dev/ and with the current API.
  • Use {{! }} in examples whenever the value could come from users.
  • Diagrams go in assets/images/ and are included with { .diagram } so they get a frame in dark mode.
  • Changes to public behaviour should update the documentation in the same pull request.

items.title: Publishing versions
items.text:
Each documentation version is a separate build, stored on the gh-pages branch by mike. The version selector in the header lists them (project.extra.version in zensical.toml). Versions are created per minor release (0.9, 1.0); a patch release redeploys its minor version. See Versioning.

Publishing is scripted in scripts/. The step-by-step instructions, the one-time GitHub Pages setup and the per-release checklist are in scripts/DOCS_PUBLISHING.md.

git checkout v1.0.0                   # release docs are built from the release tag
./scripts/publish_docs.sh --dry-run   # checks + the commands it would run
./scripts/publish_docs.sh             # build --strict, deploy 1.0, move `latest`, push
git checkout main
./scripts/publish_docs.sh --dev       # docs of the unreleased main branch

On Windows use .\scripts\publish_docs.ps1 (-DryRun, -Dev, ...). Other commands:

Command Purpose ./scripts/docs.sh serve live preview of the working tree ./scripts/docs.sh build build into site/ ./scripts/docs.sh list show published versions and aliases ./scripts/docs.sh serve-versions preview the versioned site from gh-pages locally ./scripts/docs.sh delete 0.9 remove a version

Transitional tooling

Zensical's mike fork is transitional until Zensical ships native versioning. Commands and the gh-pages layout stay compatible with mike 2.x.

items.title: GitHub Actions
items.text: .github/workflows/docs.yml publishes automatically: the dev version on every push to main, and the release version when a v* tag is pushed. Pull requests that change the documentation get a --strict build check.

items.title: Third-party code
items.text:
JoltUI bundles adapted versions of:

  • doT (MIT License), the template engine;
  • css-what (BSD 2-Clause License), the selector parser.

items.title: Package versions
items.text:
JoltUI and joltui-vite-plugin follow semantic versioning: major.minor.patch.

  • Before 1.0, a minor release may contain breaking changes.
  • The Vite plugin has its own version, independent of the framework.

Pin versions in applications and read the release notes before upgrading a minor version.

items.title: Documentation versions
items.text:
The documentation is versioned per minor release of the joltui package (0.9, 1.0, 1.1, ...). Patch releases update the documentation of their minor version.

Version Content latest (alias, default) the newest stable release X.Y the documentation as it was released with that version dev the main branch, for the next unreleased version

Use the version selector in the header to switch. Older versions stay available, so the documentation matches the version you have installed.

How versions are published is described in Writing the documentation.

items.title: AppConfig
items.text:
Passed to the App constructor.

Option Type Default Meaning appName string (required) Non-empty application name; also used by router.setTitle("_default"). dataStructure DataStructure \| null {} Shared data fields and their initial values. Only declared fields can be read or written. serverComponentsUrl string \| null null Endpoint for server components. container Element \| null null Container element, if not passed to init(). templatesCacheDuration number \| null 300 Default template-cache lifetime in seconds. templatesCacheCleanupInterval number \| null 60 Seconds between automatic cache cleanups; 0 disables them.

items.title: RouterConfig
items.text:
Passed to the Router constructor, usually in App.routerGenerator().

Option Type Default Meaning app TApp (required) The application instance. baseLayout layout class (required) Default layout; must use @layout. defaultTarget string (required) Selector inside the layout that receives the page. pages page classes generated pages Page classes; optional with the Vite plugin. baseUrl string "" Prefix for every page path; may contain <str:…> / <int:…> parameters. indexRoute string "/" Path used when the location has no path.

items.title: @component options
items.text: Option Type Meaning tagName string Required. Lowercase, starts with a letter, contains a hyphen. dataField string Re-render the whole component when this application data field changes. useServer boolean Load markup from serverComponentsUrl instead of calling markup(). groupName string Group sent with server-component requests (default "default"). cache boolean Enable template caching for the component. cacheDuration number Cache lifetime in seconds; 0 disables caching.

items.title: @page options
items.text:
@page("/path") is shorthand for @page({ path: "/path" }).

Option Type Meaning path string URL pattern; must start with /. Parameters: <str:name>, <int:name>. title string Document title, passed through titleGenerator. layout layout class Layout for this page; defaults to the router's baseLayout. target string Selector receiving the page; defaults to defaultTarget. subLayouts SubLayoutConfig[] Ordered { target, layout } chain between the layout and the page. extras Record<string, unknown> Free-form metadata, available as router.currentRoute.extras.

items.text:

Option Type Meaning useBaseUrl boolean Prepend the router's baseUrl and fill its parameters. baseParameters RouteParameters Override base-URL parameters (defaults to the current route's).

Reserved names

items.title: Decorators
items.text: Decorator Applies to Purpose @component({ tagName, … }) class Registers a custom element and its configuration. Must be closest to the class. @layout class Marks a component as a layout. Above @component. @page(path) / @page({ … }) class Marks a component as a routable page. Above @component. @auth(roles?) class Requires authentication (and roles) for a page or layout. Above @page / @layout. @lifecycle(...stages) method Runs the method at the given lifecycle stages. @handles(...ErrorTypes) method of an ErrorHandler Handles the given error types. @react(initial, binding?) accessor Reactive state; assignment refreshes binding (default: the property name). @reactFactory(factory, binding?) accessor Reactive state with a per-instance factory. @queryParam(name, default?, binding?) accessor Exposes a query parameter as a string property. @select(selector, { required? }) accessor First matching descendant. Read-only. @selectAll(selector, { required? }) accessor All matching descendants. Read-only.

items.title: Stacking order
items.text:
Decorators run bottom-up. @component registers the element and must be applied first, so it goes closest to the class:

@auth(["ADMIN"])
@page({ path: "/admin", title: "Admin" })
@component({ tagName: "admin-page" })
export default class AdminPage extends CustomElement<MyApp> {}

@auth()
@layout
@component({ tagName: "account-layout" })
export default class AccountLayout extends CustomElement<MyApp> {}

items.title: Lifecycle stages
items.text: Stage App Component Lifecycle.BEFORE_INIT ✓ ✓ Lifecycle.EXTENSION_INIT ✓ Lifecycle.BEFORE_INIT_RESOLVE ✓ Lifecycle.AFTER_INIT ✓ ✓ Lifecycle.BEFORE_RERENDER ✓ Lifecycle.AFTER_RERENDER ✓ Lifecycle.AFTER_DISCONNECT ✓

items.title: Rules
items.text:
• Property decorators (@react, @reactFactory, @queryParam, @select, @selectAll) require the accessor keyword.
  • @lifecycle and @handles decorate methods, not arrow-function properties. They cannot decorate static, private (#name) or symbol-named methods.
  • Decorators are not inherited by overrides: an undecorated override removes the registration.

items.title: Errors
items.text: All error classes are exported from joltui and can be used with @handles.

items.title: Routing and authentication
items.text: Error Raised when RouteNotFoundError No route matches the path. RouteParametersError A base-URL parameter is missing or invalid, or route parameters cannot be parsed. UnsupportedRouteParameterType A pattern uses a type other than str or int. RouteFailedError A navigation started by a link click failed (cause: the failure). AuthenticationError isAuthenticated() returned false, or a server component answered 401. Has path. AuthorizationError checkUserRoles() returned false, or a server component answered 403. Has path and roles. NotImplementedError isAuthenticated / checkUserRoles were needed but not overridden.

items.title: Components
items.text: Error Raised when ElementInitializationError A component failed to initialize. Has element, elementName, cause. MethodExecutionError An event handler or lifecycle hook threw (cause: your error). RenderError markup() threw. MissingMarkupMethod A render was requested for a component without markup. DotJSEngineError A template could not be compiled or evaluated. DependencyLoadError A lazy dependency failed to load. Has dependencyName, cause. ElementDisconnectedError A component was removed while working. Cancellation; never sent to error handlers.

items.title: Server components
items.text: Error Raised when NetworkError The request could not be completed. ServerComponentBadRequestResponse The server answered 400. ServerComponentNotFound The server answered 404. InternalServerError The server answered 5xx. HttpRequestError Any other non-success status. MarkupFetchError A 2xx response was empty or unreadable.

items.title: Wrapping
items.text:
Source Chain received by the handlers Event handler MethodExecutionError → your error Lifecycle hook during initialization ElementInitializationError → MethodExecutionError → your error markup() during initialization ElementInitializationError → RenderError → your error Link-click navigation RouteFailedError → the failure

Handlers match exact types (walking up the class hierarchy), then instanceof, then the cause. Use isElementCancellation(error) to recognise cancellation anywhere in a chain.

items.title: Events
items.text:
All events are dispatched on the app container and bubble.

Constant Event name detail When dataEventEnum.CHANGE app-data-change { field } app.setData() was called. dataEventEnum.QUERY_CHANGE query-parameter-change { field } A query parameter changed through the App. routeEventsEnum.START route-change.start — Rendering of a route begins. routeEventsEnum.LAYOUT_CHANGE_FINISHED route-change.layout-change.finished — A new base layout has been rendered. routeEventsEnum.FINISHED route-change.finished — The page has rendered and the title is set. 
this.app.addEventListener(routeEventsEnum.FINISHED, () => this.update(), {
    signal: this.abortSignal,
});

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Attribute Set by Meaning app-id App Marks the application container. data-hash-id component Unique instance identifier (hashId). data-parent-id component hashId of the component that rendered the element. data-render-time component Render timestamp; used to find freshly inserted elements. data-bind you Declares a bound region. data-bind-id template engine Identifies a bound region. data-jolt-<name> / :<name> you Component or handler argument. jolt-<event> / @<event> you Event binding. data-jolt-router-layout router Marks a sublayout element. data-jolt-layout-depth router Position of a sublayout in the chain (0 = first). router-ignore you Excludes a link from client-side routing.

items.title: Patched DOM members
items.text:
app.init() patches these members so that JoltUI templates and shorthands work everywhere inside components (details):

  • innerHTML, outerHTML setters and insertAdjacentHTML;
  • setAttribute, getAttribute, removeAttribute, hasAttribute, toggleAttribute;
  • querySelector and querySelectorAll on Document and Element.

items.title: Route parameters
items.text:
Pattern Matches Value <str:name> any single segment decoded string <int:name> digits only number

Specificity: more literal segments, then fewer parameters, then more int than str, then segment by segment (literal, int, str), then declaration order.

items.title: doT
items.text:
Syntax Meaning {{= expr }} Output, unescaped. {{! expr }} Output, HTML-encoded (&, <, >, ", ', /). {{ code }} Run statements; use /* */ comments only. {{? a }} … {{?? b }} … {{??}} … {{?}} if / else if / else. {{~ list :item :index }} … {{~}} Loop (index optional). {{## def.name: … #}} / {{# def.name }} Define / use a compile-time partial (parameterless only).

Expressions run with the component as this. Line breaks and tabs are removed before compiling.

items.title: JoltUI attributes
items.text: Syntax Expands to Meaning @event="method" jolt-event="method" Calls this.method(event, args) on the event. :name="value" data-jolt-name="value" Argument (component or handler). data-bind="binding" — Region re-evaluated when binding is invalidated. router-ignore — Link is not handled by the router.

items.title: Binding names
items.text: Binding Refreshed by app.<field> app.setData(field, …) query.<name> query-parameter changes made through the App attr.<name> changes to the host's data-jolt-<name> attribute <name> @react / @reactFactory setters, invalidate(name)

items.title: ${} versus {{ }}
items.text: ${ expr } {{= expr }} Evaluated when markup() runs on every render and region refresh Cached by the template cache yes (frozen) no (re-evaluated) Usable in data-bind regions no yes
